source_text: καὶ καταλύοντι, συναναπαυόμεθα καὶ συγκαταλύσομεν. Ἀπαιρούσῃ δὲ τῇ νεφέλῃ, συναπῆρεν ὁ λαός· καὶ καταλυούσης, συγκατηυλίζετο· «Νεφέλη γὰρ ἦν, φησὶν, ἐπὶ τῆς σκηνῆς τὴν ἡμέραν, καὶ πῦρ τὴν νύκτα.» Καταπιαίνει μὲν γὰρ ὁ Χριστὸς χαρίσμασι τοῖς πνευματικοῖς, τοὺς ὥσπερ ἐν ἡμέρᾳ καὶ φωτὶ γεγονότας, διά γε τοῦ τὴν ἐπ' αὐτῷ γνῶσιν λεπτῶς τε καὶ ἐξητασμένως ἑλεῖν, καὶ ἐκλελαμπρύνθαι τὸν νοῦν· καταφωτίζει δὲ τοὺς ἀμαθεστέρους ἔτι. Σκότος δὲ ὅλως κοσμικῆς ἀπάτης οὐκ ἔστιν ἐν Ἐκκλησίαις, περιαστράπτοντος αὐτὰς τοῦ Χριστοῦ, καὶ νοητῷ φωτὶ τὰ σύμπαντα καταυγάζοντος· οὐ γάρ ἐσμεν νυκτὸς, οὐδὲ σκότους, ἀλλ' υἱοὶ φωτὸς καὶ ἡμέρας, κατὰ τὸ γεγραμμένον. {ΠΑΛΛ.} Ὀρθῶς ἔφης. {ΚΥΡ.} Προσθέντες δὲ τούτοις, καὶ οὐκ ἐν μήκει λόγων, τοὺς ἐπί γε τῇ σκηνῇ νόμους, τάς τε τῶν λαῶν δωροφορίας, καὶ μὴν καὶ ἀπάρσεις καὶ συναυλισμοὺς, ἀφηγησόμεθα· ἴοι γὰρ ἂν οὕτω πρὸς οἶμον ὀρθὴν ὁ λόγος. {ΠΑΛΛ.} Σύμφημι. {ΚΥΡ.} Δεδικαίωκε τοίνυν ὁ νομοθέτης καὶ κριτὴς ἐν μόνῃ δὴ χρῆναι τῇ ἁγίᾳ σκηνῇ τὰς θυσίας ἐπιτελεῖν, τοὺς εἴπερ ἂν ἕλοιντο τοῦτο δρᾷν, ἀφιστὰς, οἶμαί που, τῆς ἑώλου ψευδολατρείας, τῆς ἐν Αἰγύπτῳ φημὶ, ἔνθα πολὺς μὲν ὁ τῶν εἰδώλων ἐμπαιγμὸς, θεῶν τε τῶν ψευδωνύμων ἡ ἀκαλλεστάτη πληθὺς, οὐδὲ αὐτοῖς τάχα που τοῖς προσκυνεῖν ᾑρημένοις γνωρίζεσθαι δυναμένη· ἀνεῖται δὲ καὶ τὸ θύειν, ὥσπερ ἂν ἕλοιτό τις, κατά γε τὸ ὑπό του τῶν παρ' Ἕλλησι σοφῶν ἀτημελῶς εἰρημένον, ἄλλος δ' ἄλλῳ ἔρεζε θεῶν. Ἀφιστὰς οὖν τῆς οὕτω ψυχρᾶς τε καὶ βεβήλου τριβῆς καὶ συνηθείας ἀλογωτάτης, ἔφη πάλιν ἐν τῷ Λευιτικῷ· «Λάλησον πρὸς Ἀαρὼν καὶ πρὸς τοὺς υἱοὺς αὐτοῦ, καὶ πρὸς πάντας τοὺς υἱοὺς Ἰσραὴλ, καὶ ἐρεῖς πρὸς αὐτούς· Τοῦτο τὸ ῥῆμα ὃ ἐνετείλατο Κύριος λέγων· Ἄνθρωπος τῶν υἱῶν Ἰσραὴλ, ἢ τῶν προσκειμένων ἐν ὑμῖν, ὃς ἂν, σφάξῃ μόσχον ἢ πρόβατον, ἢ αἶγα ἐν τῇ παρεμβολῇ, καὶ ὃς ἐὰν σφάξῃ ἔξω τῆς παρεμβολῆς, καὶ ἐπὶ τὴν θύραν τῆς σκηνῆς τοῦ μαρτυρίου μὴ ἐνέγκῃ, ὥστε ποιῆσαι αὐτὸ εἰς ὁλοκαύτωμα, ἢ σωτήριον τῷ Κυρίῳ, δεκτὸν εἰς ὀσμὴν εὐωδίας· καὶ ὃς ἂν σφάξῃ ἔξω ἐπὶ τὴν θύραν τῆς σκηνῆς τοῦ μαρτυρίου, καὶ μὴ ἐνέγκῃ αὐτὸ, ὥστε μὴ προσενέγκῃ δῶρον Κυρίῳ ἀπέναντι τῆς σκηνῆς Κυρίου, καὶ λογισθήσεται τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ ἐκείνῳ, αἷμα ἐξέχεεν, ἐξολοθρευθήσεται ἡ ψυχὴ ἐκείνη ἐκ τοῦ λαοῦ αὐτῆς.» Αἷμα μὲν οὖν ἐκχεῖν, καὶ τοῖς εἰς μιαιφωνίαν ἐγκλήμασιν ἔνοχον ἔσεσθαι τὸν ἔξω θύοντα τῆς σκηνῆς. Ἑαυτὸν γὰρ ὥσπερ διεχρήσατό τις, καὶ τὴν οἰκείαν ὠλόθρευσε ψυχὴν, ὁ Θεοῦ μὲν τοῦ κατὰ φύσιν ἀφιστὰς αὐτὴν, προσνέμων δὲ λίθοις καὶ ξύλοις καὶ ταῖς τῶν δαιμονίων ἀπάταις ἀνατιθείς. Ὅτι δὲ οὐ πᾶν ἁπλῶς θῦμα παρὰ τὰς θύρας ἄγεσθαι προστέταχε τῆς σκηνῆς, ἀλλ' ὅπερ ἕλοιτό τις εἰς θυσίαν ἀναθεῖναι Θεῷ, δέδειχεν ἐναργῶς προσεπάγων εὐθύς· «Καὶ οὐ θύσουσιν ἐπὶ τὰς θυσίας
pass_a_gloss: [Continuing 22: to Christ, who as in a type of the cloud departs (ἀπαίρω) from the world, we depart with him; and when he rests and lodges (καταλύω)] we rest with him (συναναπαύομαι) and will lodge with him (συγκαταλύω). The cloud departing, the people departed with it (συναπαίρω); it lodging, they camped with it (συγκαταυλίζομαι). 'For the cloud (νεφέλη) was on the tent (σκηνή) by day and fire (πῦρ) by night.' For Christ fattens / richly nourishes (καταπιαίνω) with spiritual gifts (χαρίσματα πνευματικά) those who have come to be as in day and light, through grasping (αἱρέω) knowledge (γνῶσις) of him finely and examinedly (λεπτῶς, ἐξητασμένως) and having the mind (νοῦς) made bright (ἐκλαμπρύνω); and he illumines (καταφωτίζω) those still less learned (ἀμαθέστεροι). But darkness (σκότος) of worldly deceit (κοσμικὴ ἀπάτη) is not at all in Churches, Christ flashing around them (περιαστράπτω) and lighting all things with intelligible light (νοητὸν φῶς); for we are not of night nor darkness but sons of light and day, as written. PALL: Rightly said. CYR: Adding to these, and not in length of words, we shall relate (ἀφηγέομαι) the laws on the tent, the gift-offerings (δωροφορίαι) of the peoples (λαοί, plural), and also departures (ἀπάρσεις) and encampments (συναυλισμοί); for so the discourse would go on a straight path (οἶμος ὀρθή). PALL: I agree. CYR: The lawgiver and judge (νομοθέτης, κριτής) has decreed (δικαιόω) that sacrifices (θυσίαι) must be performed only in the holy tent, by those who choose to do this, removing them (ἀφίστημι), I think, from the stale (ἕωλος) false worship (ψευδολατρεία), the one in Egypt, where much mockery (ἐμπαιγμός) of idols (εἴδωλα), and the most unlovely (ἀκαλλέστατος) multitude of falsely named (ψευδώνυμοι) gods, perhaps not even able to be known by those who chose to worship (προσκυνέω) them; and sacrificing (θύω) was let loose (ἀνίημι), as one would choose, according to the thing carelessly (ἀτημελῶς) said by one of the wise among the Greeks: 'one sacrificed (ῥέζω) to one of the gods, another to another'. Removing them therefore from so cold (ψυχρός) and profane (βέβηλος) a practice (τριβή) and most irrational custom (συνήθεια ἀλογωτάτη), he said again in Leviticus: [Lev 17:2-4 LXX] Speak to Aaron and his sons and all sons of Israel... any man of sons of Israel or of those residing (πρόσκειμαι) among you, who slaughters (σφάζω) calf (μόσχος) or sheep or goat in the camp (παρεμβολή), and who slaughters outside the camp, and does not bring (φέρω) it to the door of the tent of witness (σκηνὴ τοῦ μαρτυρίου) to make it a whole burnt offering (ὁλοκαύτωμα) or peace offering (σωτήριον) to the Lord, acceptable (δεκτόν) for odor of fragrance (ὀσμὴ εὐωδίας); and who slaughters outside [toward] the door of the tent of witness and does not bring it, so as not to offer (προσφέρω) a gift (δῶρον) to the Lord before the tent of the Lord, it shall be reckoned (λογίζομαι) to that man: he poured out blood (αἷμα ἐκχέω); that soul (ψυχή) shall be utterly destroyed (ἐξολοθρεύω) from its people. So [he says] the one sacrificing outside the tent pours out blood and will be liable (ἔνοχος) to charges of murder (μιαιφονία). For as if one did away with (διαχράομαι) himself and destroyed his own soul, he who removes it from the God by nature (ὁ κατὰ φύσιν Θεός), and assigns (προσνέμω) it to stones and wood and dedicates (ἀνατίθημι) it to the deceits of demons (δαιμόνια). That he commanded not simply every victim (θῦμα) to be led to the doors of the tent, but whatever one chose to dedicate as sacrifice to God, he showed clearly (ἐναργῶς) adding at once: 'And they shall not sacrifice upon [LXX ἔτι, 'any longer'] their sacrifices
pass_b_english: Cyril: …and lodges, we rest with him and shall lodge with him. When the cloud set out, the people set out with it; and when it halted, they camped with it (Numbers 9:17–18). ‘For the cloud,’ it says, ‘was over the tent by day, and fire by night’ (Exodus 40:38). For Christ richly nourishes with spiritual gifts those who have come to be, as it were, in day and light, because they have grasped the knowledge of him with precision and careful study and have had their minds made bright; and he enlightens those who are still less instructed. But in the Churches there is no darkness of worldly deceit at all, since Christ shines all around them and floods all things with spiritual light; for we are not of night or of darkness, but sons of light and of day, as it is written (1 Thessalonians 5:5).

Cyril: To this we shall add an account, and not at great length, of the laws concerning the tent, of the gifts the peoples brought, and also of the settings out and the encampments. For in this way our discussion would keep to a straight road.

Cyril: The Lawgiver and Judge, then, ruled that sacrifices must be offered in the holy tent alone by any who chose to offer them. He was drawing them away, I suppose, from the stale false worship, that of Egypt, I mean, where there was much mockery of idols and a most unlovely crowd of falsely named gods, a crowd perhaps unknown even to those who had chosen to worship them; and where sacrifice was left free, to be offered as anyone pleased, just as one of the Greek sages carelessly said: ‘One man sacrificed to one god, another to another.’ Drawing them away, then, from so cold and profane a habit and so senseless a custom, he said again in Leviticus: ‘Speak to Aaron and to his sons and to all the sons of Israel, and you shall say to them: This is the word which the Lord has commanded, saying: Any man of the sons of Israel, or of those who reside among you, who slaughters a calf or a sheep or a goat in the camp, or who slaughters it outside the camp, and does not bring it to the door of the tent of witness to make it a whole burnt offering or a peace offering to the Lord, acceptable as a fragrant odor; and whoever slaughters outside, and does not bring it to the door of the tent of witness, and so does not offer a gift to the Lord before the tent of the Lord, it shall be reckoned to that man that he has shed blood; that soul shall be utterly destroyed from its people’ (Leviticus 17:2–4). He says, then, that the one who sacrifices outside the tent sheds blood and will be liable to the charge of murder. For such a man has, as it were, killed himself and destroyed his own soul, since he withdraws it from him who is God by nature, assigns it to stones and wood, and dedicates it to the deceits of demons. That he did not command simply every slaughtered animal to be brought to the doors of the tent, but only whatever anyone chose to dedicate to God as a sacrifice, he showed clearly by adding at once (Leviticus 17:7): ‘And they shall not offer their sacrifices…

apparatus.note: PG OCR; column may cut mid-sentence.

Opens mid-sentence, continuing Cyril's turn from section 22 (Christ, as in the type of the cloud, departs and we depart with him; when he rests, as it were, and lodges...); the 'Cyril: …' label follows the Book 10 continuation convention. καταπιαίνει ('fattens', 'enriches') echoes section 22's image of the cloud as spiritual dew; rendered 'richly nourishes'. Numbers 9:17-18 is cited for the cloud's setting out and halting (a clear allusion; the quotation itself is Exodus 40:38 LXX). 1 Thessalonians 5:5 is quoted loosely and reordered. The line 'ἄλλος δ' ἄλλῳ ἔρεζε θεῶν' is Homer, Iliad 2.400 (Cyril's 'one of the Greek sages'); not Scripture, so no inline citation. τῶν λαῶν δωροφορίας is plural ('the peoples'), probably the tribal gifts of Numbers 7; kept as 'the peoples' and not cited. Leviticus 17:2-4: Migne omits προσηλύτων in the first clause ('those who reside among you'); in the second clause Migne reads ἔξω ἐπὶ τὴν θύραν ... καὶ μὴ ἐνέγκῃ αὐτὸ, ὥστε μὴ προσενέγκῃ (LXX: ἔξω καὶ ἐπὶ τὴν θύραν ... μὴ ἐνέγκῃ αὐτὸ ὥστε προσενέγκαι); rendered 'and so does not offer', which keeps Migne's negative without changing the sense. σωτήριον = 'peace offering' (LXX 'offering of salvation'). The quotation of Leviticus 17:7 breaks across sections 23/24; Migne's ἐπὶ τὰς θυσίας is likely a misprint for LXX ἔτι τὰς θυσίας ('no longer'); 'no longer' is not added. 'Stones and wood' is a common biblical idiom for idols (compare Deuteronomy 4:28); left uncited as a general phrase. 'Deceits of demons' may echo Leviticus 17:7 / 1 Corinthians 10:20; uncited.

changes: laws, gifts, settings out and encampments made coordinate objects of 'account' (colon implied the gifts were laws)
γνωρίζεσθαι: 'could not be told apart' -> 'unknown even to' (no added sense)
